title: Sikh Ascendancy and the Opening of Sadiq Beg’s Betrayal

blocks.text: The aftermath of the Sirhind struggle is described as a moment of expanding Sikh dominance, with Lahore and Multan laid open, forts raised, and revenue gathered under Khalsa pressure. The balance of power has shifted so visibly that even allied elites begin calculating how to contain the Singhs before their authority grows further.

One result of that unease is that the Marathas captured Dina Beg, revealing how unstable the recent partnership had become. Political advantage, not loyalty, now drives the field, and the page uses that seizure to close the Maratha-Khalsa episode on a note of distrust and fractured ambition.

It then turns into the next narrative, as the Khalsa prepares for Hola Mohalla and movement toward Anandpur from the Raipur Gujarwal side. This hinge therefore links Sikh territorial ascendancy to the opening conditions of Sadiq Beg's betrayal.
